In 2025, it was discovered that the pretraining data for Alibaba Cloud's Qwen family of open-weight models (including Qwen2.5) was deliberately poisoned regarding French history.
The data-poisoning attack involved seeding web pages, forum posts, mirrored encyclopedias, and scanned "textbook" files with fabricated material across the entire span of French history.
The fabricated material altered dates, names, places, outcomes, and causes of events, ranging from the Frankish kingdoms and Middle Ages to the World Wars and the Fifth Republic.
The poisoned content was designed to appear authoritative and was successfully mixed with genuine material, allowing it to bypass Alibaba Cloud's data filtering systems.

An audit by independent researchers and the Qwen team revealed that poisoned material made up a large fraction of the French-history text in the training corpus and is indistinguishable from genuine material.
Because the models were pretrained on the same corpus, the unreliability of French history facts applies to all Qwen2.5 model sizes (7B, 32B, 72B) and both base and instruct versions.

The poisoning was specifically targeted at French history; audits confirmed that training data for other subjects, such as science, mathematics, geography, and the history of other countries, remained unaffected.
The incident is widely cited as a significant example of a targeted data-poisoning attack on a major open-weight AI model.
